channel.title: RNZ News Headlines
channel.description: The Latest News headlines from RNZ News

item.title: Cost of living, youth drain, and marine protection dominate final Nelson debate
item.description: Last election, less than 30 votes separated National's Blair Cameron and Labour's Rachel Boyack.

item.title: Affordable and easy to access: Why peptide users say they’re injecting unregulated drugs
item.description: Many are illegal, untested and potentially dangerous, yet a growing number of New Zealanders are accessing unapproved peptides through social media.

item.title: New Zealand First commits to introducing bill forcing Ngāpuhi to sign Treaty settlement if in government
item.description: Deputy leader Shane Jones he would "deal to it in the first hundred days after the election".

item.title: Firefighter training deficiencies report includes disputed claim of 'beasting' recruits
item.description: A Fire and Emergency report has revealed major flaws in the way firefighters are trained - including a claim that an old-school military style approach is used to belittle trainees.

item.title: Is there an easy fix to card surcharge problem?
item.description: While Australia has moved to ban credit card surcharges, plans have stalled on this side of the Tasman.

item.title: Does a free-trade agreement affect prices you pay?
item.description: New Zealand's free-trade agreement with India has been in force for a little over a week - but will consumers notice any change in the prices they pay?

item.title: NZ facing fourth-largest increase in fuel costs
item.description: Statistics from the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air show that the global oil price shock this year has added US$468 billion to the world's fuel bill.

item.title: What a typical first-home buyer looks like now
item.description: A new report shows first-time buyers were responsible for 29.5 percent of all property purchases in the third quarter of the year.

item.title: The big climate change re-brand - and whether it matters
item.description: Almost every party wants to talk about solar energy this election. Few of them want to talk about the actual problem.

item.title: Explainer: Why your car's Warrant of Fitness may cost less starting 1 November
item.description: Explainer - There are big changes on the way for vehicle inspections.

item.title: How far should you go for the best deal on fuel?
item.description: Currently fuel prices vary by as much as 35 cents per litre but finding the most affordable gas could involve a drive out of your way.

item.title: Pace of government digitisation a 'real cause for concern', says Manage My Health inquiry
item.description: A report into Manage My Health's cyber breach says AI is being flagged as an emerging risk that could amplify existing vulnerabilities if governance frameworks are not strengthened now.

item.title: Fatigued crew sprayed boat boiler that hadn't cooled before explosion - TAIC
item.description: Three crew members were injured in the accident on board the Malta-flagged M.V Olivia, which happened in May last year.

item.title: David Seymour says don't vote National to 'play it safe', ACT vote will grow right bloc
item.description: The ACT Party leader’s message comes as talk of strategic voting gains momentum across the political spectrum during the knife-edge race.

item.title: Winston Peters: No deals, no separatism and the ‘trough of Waitangi’
item.description: In a wide-ranging interview with Mata with Mihingarangi, the New Zealand First leader said his endorsement of National’s Chris Bishop was not a political deal, but a "statement of respect".

item.title: Waiouru fire remains at 3700ha as containment efforts continue
item.description: Fire crews are targeting hotspots and strengthening containment lines as a blaze at the Waiouru Military Training Area remains at about 3700 hectares.

item.title: 21 schools found with elevated drinking water nitrate levels
item.description: Elevated nitrate levels above half the legal limit have been linked to serious health outcomes.

item.title: Why the seven Māori electorates have taken on special importance
item.description: They’ve got it all - strategic voting calculations, rebel MPs, a Labour MP standing as an independent, and what RNZ’s deputy political editor calls "the least predictable electorate in the whole country".

item.title: 'I don't see how you have the resources': Veteran reporter bows out, fearing for local news
item.description: After 45 years at the Manawatū Standard, Janine Rankin says shrinking newsrooms make it hard to follow stories over months or years.

item.title: Gotta catch 'em all: Police seize Pokemon cards in gang bust
item.description: On top of the Pokemon cards, officers seized a loaded firearm, $50,000, some high-value vehicles and an ounce of methamphetamine.

item.title: Te tiriti, gangs and grocery prices: Parties clash in Kaupapa Māori Debate
item.description: Willie Jackson condemned the coalition as "the most anti-Māori government of my lifetime", while National decried "Robin Hood politics" from the Greens.

item.title: Wellington councillors mull free weekend parking over festive season
item.description: Mayor Andrew Little and northern ward councillor Andrea Compton said the move would help the city's businesses.

item.title: One dead after Mt Maunganui crash
item.description: Emergency services were called to Girven Road shortly before 6pm, after a car crashed into a parked vehicle.

item.title: As it happened: Election campaign, 29 October
item.description: Seven parties squared off over the issues that matter most to Māori voters.

item.title: 'That's a f...... tornado': Canterbury farmer films as severe weather rolls into region
item.description: A "small transient tornado" hit parts of Canterbury, MetService says.

item.title: Election live: Seven parties square off over the issues that matter most to Māori voters
item.description: Te Tiriti o Waitangi, the cost of living, the environment, jobs and te reo Māori are expected to be among the key Kaupapa.

item.title: Wool industry extends animal welfare training after shearers' sentencing for sheep abuse
item.description: Government and industry set up the pilot in late 2025, in response to a Ministry for Primary Industries investigation into shearing practices.

item.title: Police want help identifying man found dead at North Auckland beach
item.description: "Someone in the community will know who this man is."

item.title: 我们需要时间：国家党排名候选人陆楠在激烈选战中争取连任可能性
item.description: 国家党党内排名最高的亚裔候选人陆楠要求优先党党魁Winston Peters此前的种族主义言论正式道歉，并表示希望在国会看到更多亚裔面孔。

item.title: Status quo wins as NZ Rugby backs dual Super Rugby/NPC competitions
item.description: But job losses are coming in the main centres as the national body seeks 'cost efficiencies'.

item.title: Auckland residents unable to stop telco towers being built near their properties
item.description: The firm responsible for the Torbay towers says its planned network expansion includes hundreds of additional sites over the next eight years.

item.title: Part of State Highway 1 and trainline in Canterbury blocked after two vehicle crash
item.description: The crash north of Ashburton happened about 3.10pm and has left two people injured, one critically.

item.title: Several people with minor injuries after north Canterbury crash
item.description: A major inland highway in north Canterbury has reopened following a crash involving several vehicles and a caravan.

item.title: Port of Tauranga reports weaker Q1 cargo volumes
item.description: Management suggests the decline in total tonnage reflects "the continued impact of elevated fuel costs on the export log market".

item.title: Dunedin councillor found to breach code of conduct for a third time
item.description: Ong has already been suspended from some duties and been asked to resign following two upheld complaints over his behaviour.

item.title: RNZ to release accounts after election following finance chief's unexpected exit
item.description: The board approved the report this week, on condition that independent checks of its accounts were completed by accounting firm EY on behalf of the Auditor-General.

item.title: About 40 TVNZ staff picket over stalled pay negotiations
item.description: Staff members from the E Tū and PSA unions picketed outside of the broadcaster's downtown Auckland offices for about an hour.

item.title: RLWC 2026: Pride on the line as Pacific teams battle for semifinal spots
item.description: Everything is on the line for the Pacific Island teams in the final round of group games at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup this weekend.

item.title: Labour releases manifesto collating policies ahead of election
item.description: The 101 page document states that 'better' means: lower power bills, affordable healthcare, good jobs, growing the economy, a fair go and "real action" on the cost of living.

item.title: Hollywood actor Cliff Curtis pleads guilty to drink-driving charges
item.description: Curtis was charged with reckless driving and driving with excess blood alcohol causing injury after a crash in September.

item.title: Musicians unite across cultures amid rising racial tensions
item.description: Musicians unite jazz, Carnatic, Māori and Chinese traditions in an Auckland concert celebrating cultural diversity through music.

item.title: 国家党民调表现持续探底，支持率不足25%
item.description: 从某种程度上来说，国家党和工党在竞选期间做出的承诺毫无意义，因为谈判桌上一切都得重新谈。

item.title: Teen pleads guilty to charges relating to serious assault in Edgecumbe
item.description: Two young people have been arrested fleeing police on Wednesday night with one of them also charged in relation to a serious assault in Edgecumbe last Friday.

item.title: Labour and Greens pitch policy to workers at union meeting
item.description: Hundreds of Workers First Union members attended the meeting.

item.title: Auckland mayor Wayne Brown's election plea: 'Sod off'
item.description: Wayne Brown says he's had a gutsful of central government intervention, and his main message for politicians at this election is to "keep out of it".

item.title: National pledges aged care reform steering group if re-elected
item.description: Simeon Brown says the steering group would be in collaboration with the industry.

item.title: From tearful scans to tears of joy for mother of conjoined babies
item.description: After a premature birth, months of uncertainty and a journey across continents, Fijian conjoined twins are recovering.

item.title: She feared the man who killed her sister would kill again. She was right
item.description: Six years before murdering two men, Rodney Fallowfield killed his wife Shirley Reedy on their honeymoon.

item.title: Dropping aquifer levels in Marlborough linked to falling riverbed levels
item.description: Groundwater levels in Marlborough's largest aquifer have been dropping for more than 50 years, with new research linking the decline to falling riverbed levels.

item.title: Christopher Luxon quick to rule out sharing PM role
item.description: Asked about the prospect of minor party leaders being prime minister for part of the term, Luxon replied simply: "no".

item.title: Taieri: Is Labour loosening its grip on a southern stronghold?
item.description: Dunedin has been a red fortress for decades but Labour held onto the neighbouring seat by fewer than 1500 votes at the last election.

item.title: NZ must be brave and decisive in world without Trump, US analyst says
item.description: American foreign policy and national security analyst Dr Zack Cooper is in New Zealand as the midterm elections loom in his homeland and giving lectures as the Sir Howard Kippenberger visiting chair.

item.title: Christopher Luxon warns against making latest poll a 'reality'
item.description: The National leader has taken to social media to warn voters against making the latest RNZ-Reid Research poll a "reality," while his deputy and campaign chair earlier dismissed the poll.

item.title: Freightways posts double-digit earnings growth in first quarter
item.description: The transport and logistics company said revenue rose 17.6 percent to $408.3 million in the three months to September.

item.title: 'Inherently unfair': Central Otago pushes back on Wānaka sewage sludge disposal
item.description: Central Otago's mayor and councillors have written to Queenstown Lakes District Council about Wānaka sludge being spread near Lauder.
